case_title: JAGDISH AND ANOTHER v. THE STATE OF HARYANA
aggravating_circumstances: Previous animosity between parties, mob assault, multiple injuries
high_court_outcome: Acquitted one accused, upheld conviction of two accused
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were neighbors with a history of animosity. The victim was assaulted at night by a group of 13 individuals. The sole eyewitness, PW1, initially made generalized allegations in the FIR but later provided more specific details in court. The victim sustained multiple injuries, including an incised wound, which the court found improbable to have been caused by only two accused. The eyewitness's credibility was questioned due to inconsistencies in her statements and the unusual circumstances of her reporting the incident alone at an unearthly hour. The prosecution relied on the eyewitness's testimony and the nature of the injuries to establish the assault, but the court found the evidence insufficient to convict the accused due to the presence of multiple assailants and the questionable reliability of the sole witness.
